title: I used Claude to port my game from Godot to Unity...in four hours! And it's 35% faster!
author: awezoomstudios
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I'm Victor, the dad of Dad and Son Games. My son and I are making Geometry Rift: Apocalypse, a neon arena shooter, survivors-like, with a campaign, big bosses and a lot of little challenges inspired by the arcade classics. We made it in Godot 4.6, and it's the kind of game where you end up with hundreds of enemies, bullets and particles on screen at the same time... so performance was always in my head.

At some point I started wondering: would the same game run better in Unity? The problem is that I don't really know Unity. I know what it is, but I never made anything serious with it, and rewriting the whole game just to find out was impossible for us.

**So I tried something a bit crazy: I asked Claude to do the port.**

To be honest I was expecting a disaster. Our game is basically one HUGE GDScript file (more than 100,000 lines, yes, I know... XD) plus around twenty smaller scripts. But Claude didn't go translating it by hand, piece by piece. It wrote a converter that turns the GDScript into C#, and a layer on top of Unity that behaves like Godot (nodes, drawing, input, files...), so the code is still our game, just in another language. Four hours later the game was running in Unity. Not one single compile error. I still can't believe it, ahahah.

And it didn't just say "done!". It recorded runs in the Godot version and played exactly the same inputs in the Unity version, to check that both games played the same. It was sick to see how it played the exact same run in both versions and compared it pixel to pixel. It was INSANE. I mean, who could have thought in comparing it like that?

https://i.redd.it/7xj4heydohyh1.png

Of course not everything was perfect. There were things Unity does a bit differently, and we found them by playing and comparing both versions side by side in the later days. One boss has four lights and Unity was only using the first one. The shockwave of another boss simply didn't draw. The red border of the danger zones was gone. And on the Steam Deck one shader read the size of a texture as zero, so a 8 bit palette became a 1 bit palette XD... All small stuff, and quick to fix. Nothing compared to what I was afraid of.

**But the really big thing was the performance. Just by porting it, without optimizing anything, the game runs about 35% faster. I**n the heaviest moments, with the huge hordes at the end of a run, it's around twice as fast. And now it runs at 60 fps on the Steam Deck, which was what I wanted the most!

https://i.redd.it/9fpk2mnmohyh1.png

And please, this is not a "Godot bad" post. I love Godot, our game was born there and I learned a lot with it. From what Claude explained to me, most of the gain comes from the code going from GDScript to C# compiled to native code, and our game is super heavy on the CPU. The one screen that depends mostly on the GPU runs the same in both engines. So if your game is not like ours, maybe you won't see the same improvement. But in my case, it was crazy.

Since a few days ago the version on Steam is already the Unity one, and we keep working on it every day.

If you have any question about how we did it, ask me and I'll answer everything I can :)

Thanks a lot for reading!

Victor. Dad.

PS: You can download the free demo here: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4701970/Geometry\_Rift\_Apocalypse/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4701970/Geometry_Rift_Apocalypse/)

comments.author: Stunning-Pizza3375
comments.body: I had the same issue with Godot being hard on the CPU - i ended up writing C++ code that Godot would execute for the heavy CPU processes. Wonder if Unity would speed things up even more 🤔

replies.author: Ianuarius
replies.body: Can't see why it would. The cap is hardware, not the engine.

comments.author: Affectionate_Fact854
comments.body:
You could use gdextention and do c++ or even rust 

You do not need to rely on gdscript for anything besides control nodes (why I'm saying control nodes is just because of how simple gdscript is to use)
